verses.1: After five days, the high priest Ananias descended, along with some elders and the messenger Tertullus. These people testified against the emperor according to what Paul had said.
verses.2: But when he was called to court, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying: “Many people have achieved peace through your efforts and by correcting the mistakes of this people.”
verses.3: We will accept it for everyone and everywhere, please, Phyllix. With all our gratitude.
verses.4: And in order that I might not have to suffer too much, I beg you, please listen carefully to our urgent requests.
verses.5: For they found this man to be contagious, and he was also causing the Jews living in their neighborhood to take certain positions. This behavior was characteristic of those who belonged to the Nazarene sect.
verses.6: Whoever also tried to defile the temple, we will also defeat him.
verses.8: And so, he must be able to recall all of these things, so that we can know what we accuse him of.
verses.9: And the Jews also wondered about this, thinking that it might be true.
verses.10: Paul also said to the governor, “After many years of being a judge among this people, I am ready to confess everything related to myself.”
verses.11: I hope you will understand that I haven’t spent more than twelve days away from Jerusalem since I first went there to worship there.
verses.12: Nor in the temple did anyone ever speak to me or question me about what I was doing. Nor among the people, nor throughout the city.
verses.13: Nor can I show you what I accuse me of now.
verses.14: I acknowledge this to you: that along the path they speak of as “a way of worshiping the Father God,” I truly do worship that Father God. I believe in everything that is written according to the law, and also in what is written by the prophets.
verses.15: With hope in God, they also expect that there will be a day when both the just and the unjust will be judged fairly.
verses.16: In this, he also possesses a constant awareness of having a relationship with the God and with all people, in every aspect.
verses.17: After many years of doing this kind of work, I managed to gain a good reputation among my people, and also received offers from them.
verses.18: In which they found me to be condemned in the temple, neither with a crowd nor with noise.
verses.19: But what about those Jews from Asia? They should be present with you, and it’s necessary to accuse them of any wrongdoing that they might have committed against me.
verses.20: Or do they say that what I did is unjust in my own court?
verses.21: Or regarding one of these voices, which I heard among them: “Today, I will judge regarding the resurrection of the dead.”
verses.22: Philex placed them in charge, knowing better about the conditions along the route. He said, “When Lysias, the commander of the troops, goes up there, I will make sure to take care of everything related to your journey.”
verses.23: It is ordered that the centurion should ensure that he has everything he needs, and that nothing is prevented from being provided for him in his personal needs.
verses.24: After a few days, Phileas, along with his own wife Drusilla, who was a Jew, sent Paul there. He listened to what Paul had to say about the faith in Jesus Christ.
verses.25: After he discussed matters related to justice, fairness, and the future punishment, Philex became very anxious. Since it’s already time for him to act now, I will send him away after waiting for the right moment.
verses.26: He also hoped that he would be given money by Paul. Therefore, he was sent away to him more tightly.
verses.27: After two years had passed, Philex Porkion became the successor. Wanting to give a gift to the Jews, Philex ordered that Paul be tied up.
